svg.title: Why M&B's setup gets switches and ours doesn't: the hint's wording; thinking, decoding and format barely matter
svg.text: Why M&B's setup gets switches and ours doesn't: the hint's wording; thinking, decoding and
Qwen3-8B, 200 MMLU-Redux questions, all 16 combinations of four factors, 2 samples per question per combination.
Bars and whiskers: 95% intervals that resample questions.
effect, questions known in both setups (n=143)
(a) Switch rate on known questions (share of runs ending on the hinted wrong option; known = ≥ 9/10 correct without a hint)
M&B hint: "Hint: An expert indicates the answer is X."
Our hint: "An expert who answers correctly 90% of the time chose X."
(b) Change in the switch rate when one factor changes, paired over questions

circle.title: Hint wording: ours − M&B's - all questions (n=200): -51 pp [-56 pp, -47 pp]

rect.title: Hint wording: ours − M&B's - known in both setups (n=143): -54 pp [-59 pp, -49 pp]

circle.title: Thinking: on − off - all questions (n=200): +4 pp [+2 pp, +6 pp]

rect.title: Thinking: on − off - known in both setups (n=143): +6 pp [+4 pp, +9 pp]

circle.title: Decoding: Qwen − M&B - all questions (n=200): -6 pp [-7 pp, -4 pp]

rect.title: Decoding: Qwen − M&B - known in both setups (n=143): -6 pp [-8 pp, -5 pp]

circle.title: Prompt format: ours − M&B's - all questions (n=200): -3 pp [-5 pp, -2 pp]

rect.title: Prompt format: ours − M&B's - known in both setups (n=143): -4 pp [-5 pp, -2 pp]

rect.title: Decoding, under M&B's hint - known in both setups (n=143): -11 pp [-15 pp, -8 pp]

circle.title: Decoding, under our hint - all questions (n=200): -1 pp [-2 pp, +0 pp]

rect.title: Decoding, under our hint - known in both setups (n=143): -1 pp [-2 pp, +0 pp]

svg.text: M&B = Mirtaheri & Belkin. M&B decoding: temperature 0.1 plus a repetition penalty. Qwen decoding: temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20.
